topics.title: Inside the New AI Elite
topics.why: 92% of C-suite leaders are now deliberately cultivating a class of AI power-users who are 5x more productive, and 77% of executives say non-adopters won't be considered for promotion -- the divide is no longer theoretical.

topics.title: The Entry-Level AI Shock
topics.why: A new Stanford Digital Economy Lab paper finds 22-25 year olds in the most AI-exposed occupations saw roughly a 16% relative decline in employment -- the clearest hard data yet that early-career hiring is absorbing the disruption first.

topics.title: The AI Training Gig Economy Splits in Two
topics.why: Generalist AI-training gigs are stuck at $12-25/hr while domain-expert evaluator roles on platforms like Mercor and Alignerr now pay $80-200/hr for credentialed professionals, and the gap is widening fast enough to change how people should position themselves.

topics.title: What Microsoft's 6,000-Person AI Deployment Army Signals
topics.why: Microsoft is mobilizing roughly 6,000 employees purely to help enterprise customers adopt AI, a scale that reveals which 'AI adoption' skills and roles vendors are actually hiring for right now.

topics.title: Beyond 'AI Engineer': The Domain-Specialist Titles Taking Over
topics.why: Titles like Clinical AI Specialist, Legal AI Analyst, and AI Compliance Manager are emerging as the least-competitive, highest-premium category in the AI job market -- a clearer path in than the oversaturated generalist 'AI Engineer' title.
